paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God doesn't just want a building, He wants to be with His people. Look at how the passage keeps landing. Moses does everything "just as the LORD had commanded him" (Exodus 40:19), and then the cloud covers the Tent of Meeting and "the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle" (Exodus 40:34). The work was never the point. The LORD coming to live among them was the point.

Now notice what happens next. Moses is unable to enter the Tent of Meeting because the cloud has settled on it (Exodus 40:35). I think that's a moment to just stand there and take a breath. Even the man who set up every last piece doesn't get to stride in like he owns the place, because the One who fills it is holy. Obedience gets the tent ready, but it's the LORD's presence that makes it matter.

And the best part is that the LORD doesn't stay put and leave them guessing. The cloud was over the tabernacle by day, and fire was in the cloud by night, "in the sight of all the house of Israel through all their journeys" (Exodus 40:38). When the cloud lifted they set out, and when it didn't, they stayed (Exodus 40:36-37). So here's what I want you to take to your own kitchen, baker: follow what God says, and let Him be the One who sets the pace. This story isn't over, either, because this is only the end of the building. There's more to come.
